description: Hi everyone! I am a software developer and cybersecurity enthusiast with a strong background in Linux systems, network architecture, and backend development. I enjoy tackling complex technical challenges and turning ideas into functional, secure prototypes under tight deadlines. You should join my team if you want a collaborative, fast-paced environment where we focus on building a solid, working product without getting stuck in endless planning.
summary: AstraForce is a web application that harmonizes 25 years of NASA MODIS (1 km, 2000–present) and VIIRS (375 m, 2012–present) active-fire hotspot data into one consistent daily record. Raw counts from the two sensors cannot be compared directly—VIIRS detects roughly 3× more hotspots for the same fires. AstraForce calibrates VIIRS to the MODIS scale using leave-one-year-out validation, ST-DBSCAN fire-event clustering, and static-source masking, so the sensor of origin no longer matters. The app serves an interactive burning-activity calendar for any region: users can draw a polygon on the map, search a place, enter coordinates with radius, or upload GeoJSON/KML. It provides daily heatmaps, month × year matrices, anomaly comparisons vs. historical median, trend analysis (Theil–Sen + Mann–Kendall), and CSV/PNG/print exports. Near-real-time FIRMS data is refreshed daily for early warning. This enables emergency responders, scientists, and land managers to examine historical fire patterns, detect unusual conditions, and identify critical burning periods.
details:
What does it do / how does it work? AstraForce is a monorepo with a FastAPI + Python 3.12 backend and a Next.js 16 frontend, backed by PostgreSQL 17 + PostGIS 3.6 + H3.

Data pipeline:

  1. Ingest: Downloads NASA FIRMS yearly country archives (MODIS Terra/Aqua, VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) and current-year NRT via the FIRMS Area API. Loads into fire_detection table with H3 r8 spatial indexing.
  2. Harmonize: Builds a static heat-source mask (gas flares, industry), clusters detections into fire events with ST-DBSCAN (1.5 km / 1 day), calibrates VIIRS to MODIS-equivalent using candidate models (monthly ratio, log-linear, Random Forest) scored by leave-one-year-out validation, and applies per country×day factors.
  3. Serve: API endpoints return daily series, month × year matrices, season dates, anomaly status, range summaries, static heat sources, and burned-area layers. The Next.js frontend renders an interactive MapLibre GL map (terra-draw drawing, Photon place search, NASA GIBS land cover overlay) and ECharts calendar/matrix visualizations.

Key features:

  • Harmonized hotspot count (default metric), fire events, and fire power (FRP)
  • GitHub-style daily calendar (2000-11 → present) + 25-year month × year matrix
  • Anomaly detection vs. 2001–present median (month, month-to-date, last 7 days)
  • Yearly ranking and Theil–Sen trend with Mann–Kendall test
  • Area selection: 6 preset countries (AZ, TR, US, AR, GR, PT), draw polygon, place search, lat/lon + radius, GeoJSON/KML upload
  • Accessible color ramps: monotonic-lightness fire, cividis (colorblind-safe), diverging blue-red anomaly
  • Exports: raw hotspots CSV, daily harmonized CSV, month × year CSV, PNG charts, printable report
  • Daily NRT refresh; provisional flags for near-real-time days

Benefits / intended impact: Emergency managers, scientists, and land managers get a consistent, sensor-agnostic view of fire activity across 25 years. They can identify peak seasons, compare current burning against historical medians, detect anomalies, and monitor sensitive regions—supporting early warning, fire response, and land-management decisions.

Tools, languages, software:

  • Python 3.12, FastAPI, psycopg 3, pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, uv
  • Node 20+, pnpm 10, Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, TypeScript
  • MapLibre GL v6, terra-draw, ECharts, @tmcw/togeojson
  • PostgreSQL 17, PostGIS 3.6, H3 (Uber hex grid), Docker
  • NASA FIRMS, NASA GIBS, Natural Earth, OpenFreeMap, OpenStreetMap/Photon

What is creative:

  • Treats VIIRS as the mean of contributing satellites per day (not a sum), avoiding false jumps when NOAA-20/NOAA-21 come online
  • Per-country calibration selected by leave-one-year-out validation with published bias metrics
  • Static-source masking removes ~25% of VIIRS industrial detections in Türkiye vs ~3% for MODIS
  • User-drawn ROIs computed atomically in SQL with heartbeat-based concurrency control

Considerations:

  • Currently limited to 6 loaded countries; new countries can be added with pnpm add-country
  • Near-real-time days are marked provisional and replaced by standard processing when available
  • Calibration is per-country; small areas inherit their country's daily factors
